findings.claim: The change edits normalizeKey, the single normalizer that ShortcutsProvider uses to dispatch every registered shortcut. No invariants file declares a touch-point list, so this shared dispatch path, and through it every Ctrl/Alt+Shift binding in core and in addons, falls outside any declared touch point.
findings.impact: Every chord pressed with Shift plus Ctrl/Cmd or Alt is now normalized differently. That covers ctrl+shift+f (GlobalSearch), ctrl+shift+k and ctrl+shift+\ (addons/knowledge Editor), and any future Alt+Shift binding. On a non-US layout, a chord whose shifted character appears in the US-keyed table is rewritten to the US unshifted face. For example, JIS Ctrl+Shift+2 produces '"', which is rewritten to ctrl+shift+'. So a binding written for a non-US key face would silently fail to match. No current binding is affected.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/shortcuts.ts:85-89 holds a table keyed by US-layout shifted characters. shortcuts.ts:107-113 applies it whenever shiftKey is held together with the primary modifier or Alt. frontend/src/components/ShortcutsProvider.tsx:81 is the only caller, and it handles every context. A grep for ctrl/alt bindings finds three Shift chords: ctrl+shift+f (GlobalSearch.tsx:166,188), ctrl+shift+k (addons/knowledge/frontend/Editor.tsx:1151) and ctrl+shift+\ (Editor.tsx:1170).

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared, so no touch-point list exists to break. The reach is app-wide through the shared dispatcher, and the only problem case needs a binding that does not exist yet.

findings.claim: The new core unit test in frontend/src/lib/__tests__/shortcuts.test.ts walks the filesystem of addons/*/frontend and frontend/src, which reaches the addon source trees from a core lib test. No touch-point list names these trees.
findings.impact: The result of a core test now depends on addon source files and on how their bindings are written. Only double-quoted `key: "..."` literals are scanned. A binding written with single quotes, a template literal or a constant is skipped without notice. A binding under a __tests__ directory is skipped as well. So the guard can pass while a real binding goes unchecked.
findings.evidence: shortcuts.test.ts (new) shiftPunctuationBindings() resolves `../addons` from the frontend root, skips node_modules and __tests__, and matches /\bkey:\s*("(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*")/g. The only guard against a vacuous pass is expect(chords.length).toBeGreaterThan(0).

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. The coupling and the narrow scan are a test-design concern, and no current binding escapes it: every current binding uses double quotes.

specification_compliance: No invariants file exists for this change, so there is no touch-point list to check against. Both places the diff reaches fall outside it: frontend/src/lib/shortcuts.ts (normalizeKey, which reaches every registered shortcut through ShortcutsProvider.tsx:81) and frontend/src/lib/__tests__/shortcuts.test.ts (which reads the addons/*/frontend source trees).
potential_unspecified_behavior: On non-US layouts, a Ctrl/Alt+Shift chord that produces a character in the US table is rewritten to the US unshifted face. For example, JIS Shift+2 gives '"', which becomes "'", and JIS Shift+; gives '+', which becomes '='. Shifted characters that are not in the table (for example JIS Shift+7, which gives "'") pass through unchanged.
On macOS, Option+Shift chords produce dead-key or special characters that are not in the table, so they are not mapped.
regression_risks: Any existing or addon binding written with a shifted character after a modifier (for example "ctrl+shift+?" or "ctrl+shift+|") would stop matching. A grep found none, but the check covered double-quoted `key:` literals only.

The existing ShortcutsProvider test (frontend/src/components/__tests__/ShortcutsProvider.test.tsx:214,218) fires key "\\" with ctrl+shift held, which is not the event a real keyboard sends. It passes either way, so it does not exercise the new mapping. This was already the case before the change.
test_coverage: shortcuts.test.ts now covers the realistic event for primary+Shift+\ (key '|') on MacIntel and Win32, plain Shift+'|' staying '|', and Ctrl+Shift+F.
The new scan-based test simulates the US-layout event for every double-quoted Shift-punctuation binding found in frontend/src and addons/*/frontend.
No test covers Alt+Shift+punctuation, a non-US layout, or the integration path through ShortcutsProvider with a realistic '|' key.
not_verified: I did not run the test suite, so I have not confirmed that the new tests pass or that __dirname resolves under the vitest config.
I did not inspect the content of commit 6dfe55339 on its own. I reviewed the diff as provided.
I did not check real browser e.key values for Cmd+Shift+\ on macOS or for JIS layouts.
I did not check bindings that are defined outside a double-quoted `key:` literal (constants, template strings, addon manifests).
